newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indosat says to hold market share.
newsitem.headline: Indosat says to hold market share.

text.p: Indonesian international telephone and satellite operator PT Indosat said on Wednesday it would keep 88 percent to 90 percent of the country's international telephone traffic in 1996.

Indosat's Executive Vice President for Marketing Bambang Sulistyo said in a statement released with the company's third quarter results that the rate at which the firm was losing market share to competitors seemed to be slowing down.

"During the nine months period of 1996, Indosat has an average 91.7 percent market share. We have projected that for 1996 we would maintain an average market share of 88 percent to 90 percent," he said.
Sulistyo claimed it reflected the company's successful effort to maintain customer confidence in the quality of Indosat's service compared to its privately owned rival Satelindo.
Indosat's international telephone traffic rose 17.6 percent to 426.6 million minutes in the nine months to September, up from 362.8 million minutes in the same period last year.
The company added 671 new international lines during the period, bringing to 6,445 the total number of international lines in operation, he said.

Indosat's President and Chief Executive Officer Tjahjono Soerjodibroto said the company estimated that by the end of 1996, it would achieve a 13 to 15 percent growth in revenues and a 12 to 14 percent jump in operating income.
